unit: one row per contig; orf_rows is one row per predicted protein
question: what are the contigs that sit far from any published protein
the_word_strain: reserved for 90-97% identity. A row at 30-45% is not a divergent strain of the taxon it is named after; the subject is the nearest neighbour in a sparse database. divergence_class states the band on every row.

bands.reading: divergent strain of the named taxon
same genus or thereabouts, not a strain
family-level or looser; the subject is a nearest neighbour, not an identification
below any band a name survives

operating_point.pfam_threshold: curators' gathering cutoffs, not an E-value of ours

the_number_to_rank_by: polymerase_pident where the contig has one, because a whole-contig best hit reports whichever gene won on bitscore. orf_identity_spread_points is how far that choice could have moved the row.
how_to_read: Compare the two arms column by column. A field that reads the same on both is describing assembly, not divergence. subject_disagreement_flag fires on a mis-joined contig AND on a genuine virus whose genes have different nearest neighbours, so read it beside evenness_within_2x_of_median and never alone.
blind_spots: An ORF with no subject and no domain is unexplained, not non-coding: past about 20-30% identity sequence search is at the end of its reach and the instrument that still works is structure, which is not attempted here
pyrodigal in meta mode calls ORFs on ribosomal and other non-coding loci; an ORF is a prediction, not an observed protein
the contigs are the study authors' assembly, so each is already a consensus and hides within-sample strain mixtures below about 3.8% divergence

the control arm is near-reference contigs from this same assembly, which shares the assembler and the library with the test arm but not its divergence; it cannot control for anything the assembler does to divergent sequence specifically
